mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the cost of capital for corporate investment and expansion.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate (above 4.5%) and rising unemployment (UNRATE increase > 0.2pp in 3 months) signals an economic slowdown under restrictive monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND UNRATE increase > 0.2pp over 3 months
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market deterioration
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met (t-test p > 0.05) or the interaction effect is not significant (interaction term p > 0.05 in a regression).

mechanism_narrative: During housing market expansions (HOUST > 1400 thousand units), increased residential construction activity and consumer spending drive economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 1400 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate indicates a tight labor market that supports higher corporate profits and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day SPX returns is < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS increase > 200k in the past month) signals robust economic activity and rising corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth > 200k (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and industrial production (INDPRO > 104) signals strong economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both conditions are met (t-test p > 0.05) or the interaction effect is not significant (interaction term p > 0.05 in a regression).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 104), manufacturing output and supply chain efficiency support corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO > 104 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
